- When sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) and model forecasts are flat or slowly rising, expect overshoot or overconfidence; adjust downward if true outcome shows sharp decline or mean reversion.
- If recent sentiment is bearish (≤0.00) and model forecasts are rising, consider lagged reaction — true price may dip after initial spike; reduce forecast slope.
- In high-event periods (≥20 events/30d) with net supply negative, model tends to underpredict peak prices; add 5–10% buffer to forecast if sentiment is neutral or mildly bullish.
- After sharp upward spikes (e.g., >10% from prior day), model often overestimates continuation; cap forecast growth at 3–5% per day unless sentiment is strongly bullish.
- If sentiment history shows repeated bearish spikes (e.g., -1.00 or 0.00) followed by model’s flat or rising forecast, expect mean reversion; reduce forecast by 2–5% for next 3–5 days.
- In high-event, high-bearish sentiment (e.g., bearish >30, bullish <15), model often underreacts to supply shocks — forecast should be 5–10% below historical mean for first 5 days.
- If model forecasts are rising steadily with no sentiment reversal, but true outcome shows sudden drop, consider “sentiment lag” — true price may dip 1–2 days after model’s peak; adjust forecast downward by 2–5% for next 3 days.
